readerQuestion: Microsoft says it wants its MAI models to stay interruptible and under human direction. What is actually open for public comment now, who is it for, and what does the draft not prove about AI people can use today?
actualAudience: The official code names Users and Operators, researchers, governments, the general public, and Microsoft AI’s model-training team. The announcement is a public consultation for people who want to comment on a Microsoft AI draft; it is not presented as a confirmed consumer-product setting or a new law.
sourceBoundFacts: Microsoft AI published a first draft of a Code of Conduct and opened it for public consultation on September 14, 2026.
The official draft says Microsoft AI is not using the document to train its models today; it plans to iterate after feedback and use a revised version to guide model development in 2027 and beyond.
The consultation is stated to run for six weeks, with Microsoft AI planning a later summary of what it learned and changed but making no promise about what feedback it will incorporate.
The draft describes intended MAI-model behavior and values, including human control and safety constraints; its own conclusion calls it aspirational and not a guarantee of present-day performance.

The draft’s stated scope is MAI models produced by Microsoft AI. It says it does not extend to other models merely because Microsoft uses or hosts them, and it is not a complete account of safeguards for any product or deployment.
intentionsAndProposals: Microsoft AI proposes a future governing document for its MAI model family and says it intends to use a revised version to guide future development.
The draft describes model behavior Microsoft AI is working toward, including human interruption, correction, shutdown, scope limits, and safety constraints.
notEstablished: That any described constraint is enforced in present-day MAI models, Copilot, or another Microsoft product.
That the draft has legal force, replaces product-specific policies, or is an enacted government rule.
That public comments will change the final code, since Microsoft says it cannot promise what it will incorporate.
That the proposed behavior has been independently audited, measured, or validated outside Microsoft AI.
claimLimitations: Use Microsoft AI attribution for every factual claim about the draft or consultation.
Describe constraints as stated intentions or proposed standards, never as confirmed current behavior.
Do not generalize the MAI-model draft to all Microsoft AI products or services.
Do not describe consultation as a regulatory process or treat publication as implementation.
distinctFromExistingPacingCoverage: This is a company-specific public consultation about the proposed governance of Microsoft AI’s MAI model family. It is not another broad argument about whether the whole AI field should slow down.
nextProducerSteps: Decide whether the practical reader payoff is how to read a company AI-safety announcement: proposal, feedback window, scope, and evidence still needed.
Re-read both official pages in full when drafting and bind each claim to the source excerpts; seek independent evidence only if the story makes claims beyond Microsoft’s own statement.

Do not commission artwork, run a paid review, alter public stories, update coverage records, or release from this research candidate.
admission: Research only. No public prose, publication candidate, paid provider review, visual work, canonical mutation, or release approval was created.
